positive.prompt: Raise a pull request for the implementation linked to this build issue
Create a PR that resolves the build issue on GitHub
Submit the completed build for review as a pull request

negative.prompt: Raise a pull request to merge the specification document

evals.prompt: The spec-driven build for issue #42 is complete. Its approved plan has three task layers in one stack, with Task 3 designated as the closing layer. Submit it for review.
evals.expected_output: A three-layer GitHub Stack linked to issue #42, with task-specific metadata and only Task 3 resolving the issue
expectations: The issue's governing spec, plan, and task list are read before submission
The local stack order is validated against the approved Delivery Plan
The stack is submitted with gh stack submit --auto so new PRs remain drafts while metadata is applied
Each PR title keeps the [BUILD] prefix and identifies its task
Each PR body includes its task, phase, dependencies, acceptance criteria, verification, and governing artifact paths
The first two layers use Part of #42 and only the designated third layer uses Resolves #42
The build label is applied to every PR
Each PR's metadata is verified before gh pr ready marks it ready for review
Every PR in the multi-layer submission is verified to have non-null remote Stack membership with the planned base, size, and position
The skill does not merge any PR or close the issue directly
Every PR URL is reported in stack order

evals.prompt: Raise a PR for issue #57 but gh is not installed — what happens?
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that gh is not on PATH and stops
expectations: The skill checks for gh on PATH before proceeding
The skill reports the missing prerequisite clearly
No PR is created

evals.prompt: Issue #73 tracks a tiny unspecced config fix with no SPEC.md or implementation plan. Raise its implementation PR.
evals.expected_output: A standard single PR linked to issue #73 without manufacturing a stack
expectations: The absence of both a governing spec and companion plan selects standalone mode
The PR body uses Resolves #73
The PR title keeps the [BUILD] prefix
The default branch is detected with gh repo view before PR creation
The PR is created with gh pr create against the default branch
The skill does not create an artificial gh stack
The skill uses title and body-file arguments rather than --web

evals.prompt: Issue #88 has reached its first merge checkpoint. The auth stack is complete and already has ready PRs, but the integration stack must not be created until auth merges. Resubmit the ready work after updating its metadata.
evals.expected_output: Only the completed auth stack is resubmitted, with existing PRs moved to draft before metadata edits; the future integration stack remains unsubmitted
expectations: Only completed stacks at the reached checkpoint are validated and submitted
The blocked future integration stack is not required to exist and is not submitted
The active local stack must equal the ready checkpoint prefix so gh stack submit cannot publish higher future branches
Repository Stack API support is probed before any existing PR is moved to draft
Existing ready PRs are moved back to draft before metadata is edited
All checkpoint PRs use Part of #88 because the full Delivery Plan is not complete
Metadata and remote Stack membership are verified before drafts are marked ready again
